page: Vultr voc-m-24c-192gb-1200s-amd is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured with 12 physical cores and 24 vCPUs via hyperthreading. The hardware includes 192.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Local storage is bundled with a 1200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark data shows strong CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core metrics placing in the top 25% of tested servers. Passmark CPU physics testing also ranks in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth and data processing benchmarks fall within the average range, including a read-only large block memory bandwidth of 141.36 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 71.93 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET throughput, which reached 42.05 million operations per second, also align with average tier performance.

The server provides high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it a qualitatively cost-effective option for memory-bound workloads that do not require specialized GPU acceleration. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores and 1200 GB of local NVMe storage supports workloads such as database hosting, memory-intensive data processing, static web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
